Subject: MAP kickoff — token model & ops assumptions (draft)

Eve / Aurelia procurement team —

Thanks for the quick sync this morning. Per our conversation, attached is a concise token-model workbook and an ops checklist I want to fold into the MAP so procurement and engineering have the same closure targets. Key pieces in the attachment:

- Baseline request profile (prompt/completion tokens per call)
- Batching & prefetch assumptions and latency impact estimates
- Prefix (session) caching assumptions and conservative savings
- Sensitivity scenarios (0.5x, 1x, 2x traffic) we can use for the SOW numbers

Immediate asks:
1) Can you confirm expected concurrent user QPS window (prod peak)? We used 100 qps for the draft but will rerun sims if you expect material differences.
2) Any strict SLA/latency requirements for the user-facing endpoint we should bake into the cost model?

I'll leave Hannah and Rishi on-thread — they own the sims and quantization/ops knobs. If procurement wants, we can export a CSV of the cost-sensitivity runs for your finance team.

Attachments: token_model_breakdown.xlsx (xlsx) — model, assumptions, and baseline sim

Thanks,
David

David — thanks for the draft. A few clarifying questions before we loop in finance: 

1) The workbook lists ~600 tokens per user request. Is that total (prompt + completion) or prompt-only? Our PM estimates are closer to 400 tokens total.
2) On caching: how often do you expect a prefix cache hit in practice for our use case (personalized follow-ups)? The draft shows 20% savings — is that conservative?
3) For batching: can you give an expected latency delta when batching to 16 vs 4 requests? We care about keeping sub-500ms tail latency.

If you can include a CSV with the sensitivity runs and an explicit line for an on-prem/private deployment (we may require it later), that would be helpful.

Eve Chen
Procurement Lead, Aurelia Health
E: eve@aureliahealth.com

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Eve Chen <eve@aureliahealth.com>, procurement@aureliahealth.com
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 13:20:10 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — token model & ops assumptions (draft)

Eve — good questions, answered inline and attached a small CSV (cache-batching-sim.csv) with the scenarios you asked for. Short answers first:

1) Tokens-per-request: the 600 in the workbook is total tokens (prompt + completion). Breakdown we used: ~350 prompt / ~250 completion. I've added a 400-token total scenario into the CSV for your PM.

2) Prefix caching: 20% was conservative for a personalized follow-up workflow with partial prompt reuse. In live pilots we've seen 15–30% depending on how much of the prompt is user-specific vs system instruction. For MAP/SOW we recommend planning for 15% (conservative), and including an optimistic 25% line in sensitivity.

3) Batching latency: empirical observations on our runtime (same-model family):
   - batch size 4: median additional latency ~8–12 ms; p95 ~30–45 ms
   - batch size 16: median additional latency ~25–40 ms; p95 ~80–120 ms

If you need to keep p95 < 500 ms overall, batching to 16 is acceptable for most of your traffic, but we should gate large batches on request soft-deadlines (we can route low-latency traffic to smaller batches). The CSV shows cost per 1M requests under the 0.5x/1x/2x traffic profiles and with/without prefix caching.

Other notes included in the attached token_model_breakdown.xlsx:
- Embedding calls: we modeled 1 embedding per user profile update (100 tokens equivalent in our sim) — that shows up as a separate line item.
- Quantization: we recommend the 4-bit quant profile for the main model in Dedicated; Rishi, I'll need your sign-off on expected latency uplift vs cost savings.
- On-prem: numbers are included but flagged as "approximate" — final SOW for private deployment will need infra sizing from your ops team.

Attachments: cache-batching-sim.csv (CSV) — 12 KB; token_model_breakdown.xlsx (revised) — 41 KB

Next steps: Hannah / Rishi can you run the 2x traffic stress sim and post results to the Drive link? I'll update the MAP doc and SOW draft once we confirm concurrency.

Thanks,
David

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 03 Nov 2025 15:05:22 -0700
Subject: Fwd: MAP kickoff — token model & ops assumptions (internal notes)

Forwarding Eve's questions with quick internal checks. Short internal notes: 

- Concurrency assumption: David used 100 qps baseline. For stress sim we should run 50 / 100 / 200 qps and include dedicated GPU parity (2x A100-ish equivalence) as an ops fallback in the MAP. The cost delta at 200 qps shows batching benefits increase but so does queueing tail latency — we need routing rules.
- Caching: set conservative hit-rate to 15% in the official MAP table; add optimistic 25% line in the appendix so finance sees upside.
- Sensitivity: include token-size variance +/- 25% rows (so 450–750 tokens). That will give procurement clear low/likely/high cost buckets.

Rishi — can you add one more column to cache-batching-sim.csv with "quant-profile = 4-bit" vs "8-bit" latency and cost estimates? I'll run the 2x traffic sim tonight and push results to the Drive.

Hannah
Sr. Product Ops, Redwood Inference

2) Call out the routing fallback policy: if p95 > 750ms, route to the fallback model (include expected quality delta in appendix).
3) Add the Drive and HubSpot links to the MAP header. HubSpot: HS-32844.

Once Rishi and Hannah post the finalized CSV & sims, David — please export the one-page summary and attach to the MAP email to Aurelia. Procurement will expect the attachments and the single-page to match line-for-line with the numbers in the SOW they send to finance.

Laura Bennett
